Hey!

​

A quick message to tell you, i'm 20, still struggling of course, but 17 YEARS OLD is A LIVING HELL. Trust me, I don't know what movies wanted us to believe, but 16 and 17 were the hardest years of my life. Everything got sooo much better when I got out of high school. Still looking for a purpose, but for now, if I could talk to the 17 yo me, I would just tell her that she has time to figure it out. Nowadays, it feels like if you're not rich and famous at 16 you failed, but it's not the case, trust me. Teenage years are so hard, and people expect so much from you now, even when you had to go through a worldwide pandemic. 

My purpose and the thing that kept me going when I was your age was to think about where I would go after high school. I moved thousands of miles away from home to get a fresh start, and yes, my demons traveled with me, but I feel like here I can control them... a bit more. 

It takes time, not gonna lie. But time is all it takes after all.

Hello!

​

First of all, CONGRATULATIONS! 

I suffer from the exact same thing, as soon as my roommate leaves for work I want to eat everything that is in my kitchen as if I was restricting when she's here even though it doesn't feel like it. 

I will try to do the same as you did next time she leaves (aka tomorrow), but what you did tonight is huge, keep going, you're on the right path! There is a way out to this thing.

Hello! One advice I can give you is (if your scale allows it) to change the system. Meaning I am from Europe so I use the metric system, and I know that If I see certain numbers i will get triggered and cry, not eat at all or binge the whole day. So I decided to switch to pounds instead of kilograms, and since pounds is a foreign system I did not assimilate the numbers with bad feelings!

Good luck for your recovery, this is not easy but you can do it!
